name: Commons at Mosaic
headline: Archway is turning Gaebe and Triangolo Halls, two vacant former Johnson & Wales dorms on Denver's Mosaic Community Campus in South Park Hill, into 58 apartments on Denver Housing Authority land: 31 supportive homes with vouchers for people leaving homelessness and 27 family homes at 40% to 60% AMI. It won 2026 Round One federal 9%, state and TOC credits.
why_it_matters: It is a model for supportive housing on housing-authority land. DHA bought the buildings with city D3 money and sells them to Archway for a nominal price on a 99-year ground lease. A seller carryback note covers the full building value, which also earns acquisition credits, alongside federal and state historic credits.

status.label: Credits awarded; closing and construction start not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA lists the award as of 2026-09-30. The applicant aimed to close in fall 2026 and start construction in 2026; an earlier Archway/DHA release said renovations would begin in early 2027. There is no public closing, permit or groundbreaking record.

next_step: Watch for the financing closing and the Denver building permit, and for the DHA board's approval of the final ground lease and building transfer.

background.text: In June 2021 the Urban Land Conservancy, Denver Public Schools and DHA bought the 25-acre former Johnson & Wales campus at Montview Boulevard and Quebec Street. It is now the Mosaic Community Campus.

Phase one: Archway converted four other dorms into 154 affordable family units, opened in fall 2024 and fully leased. For that phase, a $3.85M HOST loan carrying a 60-year covenant went to a Denver City Council vote set for 2022-12-19.

DHA used D3 resources to buy the South Campus buildings for future supportive housing. D3 rules require at least 40% of the units to be supportive housing with vouchers, and this project has 31 of 58.
Site control is an Agreement for Building Transfer and Ground Lease with DHA. Archway buys the buildings for a nominal value and takes a 99-year ground lease at nominal cost.

Unit plan: Gaebe Hall has 20 one-bedroom, 7 two-bedroom and 4 three-bedroom units, all at 30% AMI or below. Triangolo Hall has 17 one-bedroom, 6 two-bedroom and 4 three-bedroom units: 3 at 40%, 14 at 50% and 10 at 60% AMI.

Rehab scope: interior conversion of the 1930s-era masonry dorms with exteriors unaltered. Work includes new stretcher-size elevators in rebuilt cores, extensive asbestos abatement and new plumbing and electrical. The project follows Enterprise Green Communities.
The buildings are vacant, so no one needs to be relocated. The applicant says DHA's D3 acquisition is the only prior public investment in the property.

Archway submitted its development proposal to the city in November 2025. At application, design development drawings were 100% done and the project was in review with Denver's affordable housing review team (AHRT).
Archway and DHA held a community meeting on the campus on 2025-11-05, where the District 8 council member spoke in support.
The market study put the overall capture rate at 29.2%, with 74.3% for the 60% AMI units. Archway plans to discount the 60% AMI rents to help lease-up.

discrepancies.text: An Archway announcement reposted by CHHSM says the project received $2.72 million in housing tax credits, including federal 4% credits, while CHFA's award report lists $1,800,000 federal 9%, $500,000 state and $116,000 TOC credit (together $2,416,000), with no 4% award.
The 2026 application narrative targets closing and construction start in 2026 (closing in fall 2026), while the 2025 Archway and DHA announcement aimed to begin renovations in early 2027.

CHFA's award description lists 36 one-bedroom and 14 two-bedroom units; the application narrative's building-by-building plan adds up to 37 one-bedroom and 13 two-bedroom. The bedroom mix shown uses the award description.
